primitives.name: First Month Review Queue
primitives.verbatim_quote: # First Month Review Queue Export Updated: 2026-07-05 Status: local review export only.
primitives.assumptions: (1) All content undergoes a mandatory 30-day internal review cycle; (2) Drafts flagged as unsafe remain blocked and require manual repair; (3) Exported packets are never published, sent to external partners, or integrated live until approval.

layer2.mapping: The review queue acts as a formal safety filter that enforces a publishAllowed=false gate, aligning with GSI's claim-safety verification pipeline and GSE's workflow fence protocols. It ensures all content meets the safety contract before any owner decision is made.
layer2.telemetry: Number of blocked packets, claim-blocked items, and evidence-required drafts per batch

primitives.name: Content Fixture Plan
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Purpose The first-month review queue export turns the 30-day content fixture plan into local review packets.
primitives.assumptions: (1) The fixture plan defines a fixed 30-day window; (2) Each packet corresponds to a specific day and week within this window; (3) The transformation process is deterministic and lossless.

layer2.mapping: The fixture plan serves as the foundational input to the review queue, providing the temporal scaffolding for GSI's content scoring and GSE's cadence coverage metrics. It bridges strategic planning to operational execution.
layer2.telemetry: Packet generation rate, script-beat count distribution, and content score variance across the 30-day period

primitives.name: Safety Contract
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Safety Contract Every exported packet keeps: - `publishAllowed: false` - `externalSendAllowed: false` - `routeExposureAllowed: false` - `liveIntegrationAllowed: false` Unsafe drafts can be represented in the queue, but they remain `BLOCKED` and waiting on repair.
primitives.assumptions: (1) The safety contract is an immutable constraint enforced at the packet level; (2) Blocked drafts are isolated from all external flows; (3) Repair is a sequential process that transitions a draft from BLOCKED to APPROVED.

layer2.mapping: The safety contract implements a veto layer that mirrors GSI's claim-safety framework, preventing unsafe content from reaching GSE's workflow fences. It ensures compliance with both internal and external regulatory standards.
layer2.telemetry: Proportion of packets in BLOCKED vs. APPROVED states, and average time-to-repair per draft

primitives.name: Export Contract
primitives.verbatim_quote: returns: - 90 local review packets by default - generated timestamp - blocked packet count -
primitives.assumptions: (1) The export produces a fixed-size batch of 90 packets; (2) The generated timestamp anchors the review cycle; (3) Packet counts are additive and non-negative.

layer2.mapping: The export contract specifies the output interface for the review queue, defining the telemetry required by GSE's monitoring systems and the data structure consumed by GSI's content scoring algorithms.
layer2.telemetry: Batch size consistency, timestamp drift, and cumulative blocker counts over multiple export cycles
